topics.quote: Yeah onboarding is not paid. If it’s in your contract, read carefully. It’s only after you submit your first task and it’s approved.
topics.summary: The poster asks whether onboarding is paid if they quit before submitting work; commenters disagree, with some saying payment requires a first task and approval.

topics.quote: I find it more probable that they are just not organized enough to get it approved for Gatekeeper.
topics.summary: A Mac security warning about the required Task Recorder prompted speculation about malware and data misuse, while others said the app was safe or suggested a less sinister explanation; the allegations are unverified.

topics.quote: i offboarded myself because i was invited to be a reviewer and even after answering correctly to the quiz questions i still failed, which prevented me from becoming a reviewer.
topics.summary: One worker says they failed a reviewer-entry quiz despite answering correctly and left the project.

topics.quote: Honestly, every offer now seems to be wildly different so it might actually be right.
topics.summary: Workers report differing payment structures, including $50 an hour for up to five onboarding hours and a claimed unusually large first-task offer.

topics.quote: I received an hourly rate but no task rate at all. But I can't find any AHT information on how long a task should take to complete.
topics.summary: Workers report unclear task timing, difficulty installing a required program because of a Mac security warning, and dissatisfaction with the project.

topics.quote: I got onboarded yesterday and the contract was paused today morning lol
topics.summary: One worker says their contract was paused the morning after onboarding, and another describes the project as oversaturated.

topics.quote: Another rejection
topics.summary: The title reports another rejection, without saying who was rejected.

topics.quote: My Contract got Revoked
topics.summary: The poster says their Mercor contract was revoked.

topics.quote: 2 years on mercor, never even got a single project
topics.summary: The poster reports getting no projects in two years, while another commenter reports five projects in two months and another says they received instant offers.

topics.quote: Did ok on the quiz and was rejected.
topics.summary: Commenters describe assessments and applications, with some receiving offers and others reporting rejection or no selection.

topics.quote: The instructions were hard to access for everyone, the UI was tacky and they didn’t clarify what they wanted us to distinguish.
topics.summary: A commenter says an assessment had inaccessible and unclear instructions and a poor interface.

topics.quote: Even the ideation sounds like the same excel M slop.
topics.summary: The poster is struggling to come up with workflow ideas for Project O and finds its ideation repetitive.

topics.quote: Currently on project V...LOL never accepting a low pay offer again.
topics.summary: The poster says their current project pays poorly and cautions others about accepting low-paying offers.

topics.quote: Mercor has paused my contract after flagging a 13.3-hour Insightful session, along with two other sessions of 6.4 and 6.1 hours.
topics.summary: The poster's long tracked sessions were flagged and their contract paused, while another worker reports logging similarly long sessions without a pause or deduction; commenters disagree about how strictly breaks must be excluded.

topics.quote: Mercor has paused my contract after flagging a 13.3-hour Insightful session, along with two other sessions of 6.4 and 6.1 hours.
topics.summary: Mercor paused the poster's contract pending an explanation, and commenters offer conflicting predictions about reinstatement versus offboarding; the thread does not establish the outcome or review time.

topics.quote: I have had sessions that long (I ADHD hyperfocus) and I get canned for AHT, not the sessions.
topics.summary: One worker reports being removed over average handling time, and commenters say unusually long task times can trigger checks even when the work is difficult.

topics.quote: Received an offer but no further onboarding instructions
topics.summary: The poster received an offer but no further onboarding instructions.

topics.quote: I just got a rejection 😔
topics.summary: The poster asks whether anyone joined the Healthcare Survey Research & Pharma Insights Expert project, and a commenter says they were rejected.

topics.quote: Received the same email on Tuesday, completed their request within 30 minutes and I’ve heard nothing since completing it.
topics.summary: People report being accepted, rejected or left waiting after applying, while giving conflicting information about which Macs and macOS versions qualify; onboarding includes reading, ID checks and software setup.

topics.quote: Im quite happy tbh with the role except for communication which sucks.
topics.summary: Project Odin involves proposing tasks in one's area of expertise and recording oneself completing them; some find it straightforward, while others are confused, dissatisfied or have quit.

topics.quote: It takes some time to set-up the infra and generate task ideas (all upaid) and you do not get paid until the task is approved.
topics.summary: One worker reports unpaid setup and ideation, payment contingent on task approval and a three-hour weekly cap, while another says time tracking can start once the tracking app is installed and a commenter has heard onboarding is now paid.

topics.quote: they also changed payment from per $50/task $40/hour which is better but capped at 3 hours per week.
topics.summary: A worker calls the pay good, another reports a change from $50 per task to $40 an hour with a three-hour weekly cap, and commenters mention higher pay for Intel Macs and a possible $250 approval bonus.

topics.quote: I've seen some things about possible security concerns involving the app used to screen record on the Mac, and how it triggers the internal warnings.
topics.summary: Commenters question whether the project is legitimate, raise possible security concerns about its screen-recording app and express discomfort about a contract clause concerning side work.

topics.quote: I also got a referral payment for referring someone to the platform, and they paid exactly when they said they would.
topics.summary: One participant says a referral payment arrived on time and that their partner and friends were also paid on time, though their own first project payment had not yet arrived.

topics.quote: Im quite happy tbh with the role except for communication which sucks.
topics.summary: A worker criticizes project communication, and another commenter alleges that reviewers avoid explaining their review protocols.

topics.quote: They identify themselves as reviewers, but if you ask them about how and what protocols they use to review the submissions, they just ignore completely and put the whole blame on the writer.
topics.summary: A commenter alleges that reviewers do not explain their protocols and blame writers, while a worker says tasks must be approved for payment.
